insights_with_evidence.claim: 好的设计应通过可发现性（示能、意符、约束、映射、反馈、概念模型六大理念）让产品无需说明书即可理解，简单东西需要说明书就是设计失败。

evidence.excerpt: A good product should be easy to understand without a manual. Norman calls this **discoverability**, and he says good discoverability comes from six key ideas.

"When affordances are taken advantage of, the user knows what to do just by looking [...] Complex things may require explanation but simple things should not. When simple things need pictures, labels or instructions, the design has failed."

insights_with_evidence.claim: 诺曼的设计哲学核心是人性化信念：用户不应为日常物品的使用失败感到愚蠢，失败的责任归于设计而非用户。

evidence.excerpt: Norman's principles are not about fancy theory — they are about something simple and human: we should be able to understand everyday things without feeling stupid.

Donald A. Norman's goal is to help relieve feelings of incompatibility by putting the blame on the poor design of everyday things in our environment rather than on ourselves. When we fail to deal appropriately with our environment of water faucets, doors, and VCRs, we usually blame ourselves.

When we fail to deal appropriately with our environment of water faucets, doors, and VCRs, we usually blame ourselves. Norman demonstrates that much of the blame should be placed on the designer

Most accidents are attributed to human error, but in almost all cases the human error was the direct result of poor design. The principles that guide a quality, human-centered design are not relevant just to a more pleasurable life—they can save lives.

Good design will not remove the difficulties and challenges of everyday life. As members of Homo curiousitus, we seek out challenging and difficult puzzles to solve. Good design of everyday things will give us more time to confront things in a more meaningful and fulfilling way.

insights_with_evidence.claim: 增加功能通常以增加复杂性为代价。诺曼后期从设计单个产品转向设计系统，关注复杂性而非简单性。

evidence.excerpt: Added functionality generally comes at the cost of added complexity.

Since 2010, Don Norman, author of The Design of Everyday Things, has shifted (or re-shifted) his focus from designing individual products to designing systems. Living with Complexity (2010) focused on dealing with the complexity of reality and course correcting from a focus on simplicity. His forthcoming book, Design for a Better World (2023), takes the scale even larger to focus on how individual design choices are coupled with larger systemic effects.

insights_with_evidence.claim: 诺曼承认在设计领域误用'affordance'概念：他实际讨论的是'perceived affordance'而非Gibson意义上的真实affordance。在图形界面中，设计师只能控制感知到的示能，他计划在修订版中替换全部术语。

evidence.excerpt: I should have used the term "perceived affordance," for in design, we care much more about what the user perceives than what is actually true. What the designer cares about is whether the user perceives that some action is possible (or in the case of perceived non-affordances, not possible).
In graphical, screen-based interfaces, all that the designer has available is control over perceived affordances.

To my great surprise, the concept of affordance was adopted by the design community, especially graphical and industrial design. Alas, yes, the concept has caught on, but not always with complete understanding. My fault: I was really talking about perceived affordances, which are not at all the same as real ones.
POET was about "perceived affordance." When I get around to revising POET, I will make a global change, replacing all instances of the word "affordance" with the phrase "perceived affordance."

insights_with_evidence.claim: 违反惯例的设计即使更优越也注定失败。诺曼强烈主张遵循既有用法，尊重文化惯例，因为惯例虽看似随意实则经过演化积淀，一旦采纳就难以改变。

evidence.excerpt: Those who violate conventions, even when they are convinced that their new method is superior, are doomed to fail.

Conventions are not arbitrary: they evolve, they require a community of practice. They are slow to be adopted and, once adopted, slow to go away. So although the word implies voluntary choice, the reality is that they are real constraints on our behavior. Use them with respect. Violate them only with great risk.

How do you know if the user shares the conventions? Why, with data, of course. This is something that cannot be decided by arguments, logic, or theory. Cultural constraints and conventions are about what people believe and do, and the only way to find out what people do is to go out and watch them—not in the laboratories, not in the usability testing rooms, but in their normal environment.

insights_with_evidence.claim: 诺曼区分物理约束（与真实示能相关）、逻辑约束（推理确定选项）和文化约束（习得的共享惯例）三类行为约束，强调必须明确区分使用场景。图形设计中的大量'affordance'实际是文化约定。

evidence.excerpt: In all scrolling bars I have seen, there is a physical constraint as well: the vertical scroll bar only moves vertically, not horizontally. All this is cultural convention, not affordances.

In POET, I introduced the distinctions among three kinds of behavioral constraints: physical, logical, and cultural. These are powerful design tools, so let's be clear where each is being used. Physical constraints are closely related to real affordances... Logical constraints use reasoning to determine the alternatives... Cultural constraints are conventions shared

insights_with_evidence.claim: 诺曼以三里岛核事故调查为转折点，从认知科学家变为设计倡导者：发现操作员并无过错，根本原因是控制室设计缺陷——控制面板像是'故意设计来导致错误的'。

evidence.excerpt: To my surprise, we concluded that they were not to blame: the fault lay in the design of the control room. Indeed, the control panels of many power plants looked as if they were deliberately designed to cause errors.

We decided that the operators were really quite intelligent and sensible and everything they did was sensible except that the design was so bad that if you wanted to cause people to make errors, you couldn't have done a better job. There were 4000 meters and controls laid out in a neat orderly way, so that you might have a bank of 20 switches and then if you flipped on in the middle wrong, people got mad at you.
evidence.source_file: exa_7_Transcript_ A Chat with Don Norman.md

insights_with_evidence.claim: 诺曼的生活哲学是持续向前：从不回头看已完成工作，每年学习一个新主题，喜欢教和讨论自己不理解的东西，理解后就写书转向下一个主题。

evidence.excerpt: I never look back at the stuff I've done. I look forward to where I'm going. [...] If I don't do a dramatically new thing each year and learn a new topic, then I'll stagnate. It's part of my philosophy of life, to always push off in different directions.

What I'm going to do is stumble through what I'm thinking about. That's what I really like to do. I like to teach and think and talk about stuff I don't understand. And so I give crappy talks because I'm making it up as I go along. And when I do understand it, I write a book and then I'm bored with it and go on to the next topic.

insights_with_evidence.claim: 诺曼在Apple经历后从批评设计师转变为理解设计约束：认识到没有'愚蠢的决定'，糟糕设计源于孤立解决问题，必须同时考虑国际市场、价格、兼容性等。

evidence.excerpt: I actually very much remember my encounter with you, John, because I think you were the first real designer I ever met. [...] I realized that maybe I didn't understand the problems that designers face.

There are no "dumb decisions." Everybody has a problem to solve. What makes for bad design is trying to solve problems in isolation, so that one particular force, like time or market or compatibility or usabilility, dominates.

I've really come to appreciate the pressures put on design. [...] We have to worry about the international market, we have to worry about price, we have to worry about compatibility with the partners. So I've really come to broaden my appreciation for what goes on, which, in turn, increases my admiration for those good designs that are eventually produced.

insights_with_evidence.claim: 诺曼提出'认知工程学'：将科学知识应用于机器设计，目标不是效率而是令人愉悦的系统（'愉悦参与'）。正确概念模型可将困惑困难的任务转化为简单直接的任务。

evidence.excerpt: Cognitive Engineering, a term invented to reflect the enterprise I find myself engaged in: neither Cognitive Psychology, nor Cognitive Science, nor Human Factors. It is a type of applied Cognitive Science, trying to apply what is known from science to the design and construction of machines.

To devise systems that are pleasant to use—the goal is neither efficiency nor ease nor power, although these are all to be desired, but rather systems that are pleasant, even fun: to produce what Laurel calls "pleasurable engagement"

the comment reveals the power of the proper conceptual model of the situation: The correct conceptual model can transform confusing, difficult tasks into simple, straightforward ones. This is an important point that forms the theme of a later section.

insights_with_evidence.claim: 设计师不直接与用户对话——所有沟通通过'系统映像'（system image）进行。如果系统映像不能清晰传达设计模型，用户就形成错误的心理模型。

evidence.excerpt: The designer expects the user's model to be identical to the design model. But the designer doesn't talk directly with the user—all communication takes place through the system image. If the system image does not make the design model clear and consistent, then the user will end up with the wrong mental model.

insights_with_evidence.claim: 诺曼认为设计界已理解如何做出好产品但糟糕设计仍大量存在，问题不再是新理论而是教育。他已对可用性工作厌倦，转向情感化设计：让产品不仅实用更令人愉悦有趣。

evidence.excerpt: I believe that we now do understand how to design so that the result truly fits people. [...] Lots of individual designers are still hopelessly inept. [...] having worked to make products easier to use for the past 15 years, I am getting bored.

evidence.excerpt: A theory of action is outlined in which an action sequence is represented by a parent schema and numerous child schemas, in which several action schemas can be active at any one time, and in which each schema has a set of triggering conditions and an activation value. A slip is the error that occurs when a person does an action that is not intended.

Most slips
have multiple causes. Many sources of
information are likely to be interacting
to give rise to any particular action.
When the act
is an error, it is apt to be the result of nu-
merous underlying forces, so that the re-
sulting slip is multiply determined and con-
sistent with a number of constraints and
explanations.

The proposed model, an activation-trig-
ger-schema system (ATS), assumes that
action sequences are controlled by sensori-

skilled—need only be specified at the highest

sequence complete the action, to a large ex-

with the information processing distance between
the user's intentions and the facilities provided by the ma-
chine. Reduction of this distance makes the interface

In a system built on the
conversation metaphor, the interface is a language medium in which the
user and system have a conversation about an assumed, but not explicitly rep-

the user and the world about which things are said. In a system built on the
model-world metaphor, the interface is itself a world where the user can act,
and which changes state in response to user actions.

We suggest that the feeling of directness is inversely proportional to the
amount of cognitive effort it takes to manipulate and evaluate a system and.
moreover, that cognitive effort is a direct result of the gulfs of execution and
evaluation. The better the interface to a system helps bridge the gulfs, the less
cognitive effort needed and the more direct the resulting feeling of interaction.
